clue.text: Order sponge that's cut or a piece of cake inside cafe

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, so the easy piece goes into the shuffled letters
to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new arrangement
a word that is cut has lost its tail, so the last letter of the sponge goes

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes
taken as written
a piece of cake is something easy

explanation.surface: Someone in a cafe orders sponge cake, or a slice of some other cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a customer ordering food, but it signals the rearrangement; 'piece of cake' is not food either, but the idiom for something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is British slang for a cheap, basic cafe serving fried food.

clue.text: Badger poacher with gun dealt reward at the end

indicators.note: to badger is to harass or pester, so these letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A poacher armed with a gun is handed a final payoff, with a badger caught up in the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal a poacher might hunt, but here it is a verb signalling the anagram of POACHER, GUN and DEALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden parachute is a large payout given to an executive when they leave a company.

clue.text: Live in sun during retirement

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so the sun goes inside

parts.note: retiring from a scene is making an exit

explanation.surface: Someone spends their retired years living in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, so the verb is a synonym for live.

clue.text: Keep to right entering last passage

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it, so the right letter goes into the keep word

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to keep a deleted word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep to the right on entering the final corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet is the proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand', a common crossword way to clue keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretto is the closing section of a fugue or piece of music, played faster, so a final musical passage.

clue.text: Very neat in retrospect after biro's beginning to dry out

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the biro letter in the answer

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of biro is used
looking back reads the word from its end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: neat spirit is pure, undiluted

explanation.surface: Neat drinking is looked back on after a pen is used to sign up for drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is the drinker's word for an undiluted spirit, which is why it gives pure here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to stop being drunk, which is what drying out means for a drinker.

clue.text: Topless shoot that's red hot

parts.note: a topless car or bus is open, with no roof
fire is red hot

explanation.surface: A topless photo shoot that turns out to be extremely racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' reads as a photo shoot, but it is the verb meaning to fire a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To open fire is to begin shooting with guns.

clue.text: Region died: toxin released poisonous gas

indicators.note: letters released from their order are free to fall into a new one

explanation.surface: A toxin let loose in a region killed people: a poisonous gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen dioxide is a toxic brown gas produced by combustion and a major air pollutant.

clue.text: Massaging sporty hip, yeah?

indicators.note: massaging works and kneads something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the treatment for an athlete's hip will be massage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram of SPORTY HIP YEAH and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiotherapy treats injuries such as a sportsperson's hip with massage and exercise.

clue.text: Film in April, May and June?

definitions.text: Film in April, May and June?

parts.words: Film in April, May and June?
parts.note: April, May and June are both months on a calendar and girls' names, pointing to a 2003 British film title

explanation.surface: A question about what film is showing in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Calendar Girls is a 2003 film about Yorkshire Women's Institute members posing for a charity calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The months April, May and June are also female names, so they are girls found in a calendar.

clue.text: Hospital patient's heart to pound; one in bed, perhaps is not so flat

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
someone lying in bed is a lier

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's heart pounds while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes I, the middle letter of 'patient's' (ignoring the apostrophe).
explanation.definitionFit: Hillier is the comparative of hilly, describing ground with more hills and less level land.

clue.text: Drink running water with live newt further up

indicators.note: the other pieces sit further up, ahead of the river piece in the answer

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
an eft is a young newt
ea is a dialect word for a river or running water

explanation.surface: A drink of river water with a live newt in it.
explanation.walkthrough: EA, a dialect word for a river, is a crossword staple; 'further up' puts BE and EFT before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a hot broth made from beef, traditionally given to invalids.

clue.text: Harry Potter cast shortly watching one

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are thrown into a new order
cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: The Harry Potter cast, briefly, watching someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is not the boy wizard but the anagram signal; 'shortly' cuts CAST to CAS, rearranged with POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is a person who looks on at an event.

clue.text: Stopped in Australia, mostly at large houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: an escaped prisoner at large is free
Oz is an informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A traveller paused in Australia, mostly staying at big houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' reads as a noun for big homes, but it is the verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Froze means stopped dead or became motionless.

clue.text: Silly me loves writing puzzles after vacation!

indicators.note: the loves are written down beside the following pair of letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero

indicators.note: a word vacated has its insides emptied, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone who loves writing puzzles admits a gaffe after their holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' reads as a holiday, but it means emptying 'puzzles' to leave PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is what one says on making a silly mistake, an exclamation like silly me.

clue.text: Cold-blooded American being busy leader

parts.note: busy is old British slang for a police detective, as is copper
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A ruthless American who is a busy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is old British slang for a policeman, and 'Cold-blooded' points to a reptile rather than a callous person.
explanation.definitionFit: The copperhead is a venomous North American snake, and snakes are cold-blooded reptiles.

clue.text: Where desires are titillated by top-shelf bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Top-shelf magazines with a bust on the cover titillate desires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-shelf' means pornographic in Britain, sold on the top shelf; 'bust' is the anagram signal, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshpot is a place offering sensual pleasures, such as a sleazy nightclub or red-light district.

clue.text: Does one tend to watch hot girls soon to get stripped off

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
a word stripped loses its outer letters, leaving only the middle

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a man ogles attractive women who will soon undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get stripped' takes OO from SOON; 'off' then rearranges HOT, GIRLS and OO. 'watch' is a timepiece, not looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A horologist studies or repairs clocks and watches, so tends to a watch.

clue.text: Family man with pretty secretary

parts.note: grand and pretty can both mean fine or nice
PA, a personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A married man with a good-looking secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandpa is a grandfather, a male relative in the family.

clue.text: Sign accordingly giving envelope for my foreign letter

indicators.note: giving an envelope to letters wraps the outer word round them

parts.note: so means therefore, accordingly
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A signature on a letter abroad, sent in a suitable envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise, much like 'my!'; the foreign letter is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old designer leaving Italy to make scent for Americans

indicators.note: the Italy letter leaves, so it is removed from the designer

parts.note: Dior is the French fashion designer
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A veteran fashion designer leaves Italy to make perfume for the US market.
explanation.definitionFit: Odor is the American spelling of odour, meaning a smell.

clue.text: Female, not in dresses, stuns

indicators.note: the female letter is not in, so it is taken out

parts.note: frocks are dresses

explanation.surface: A woman in dresses is a stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks means shakes or stuns, as news rocks a community.

clue.text: With a better argument, American Mancini ultimately pens 'keep Moon River'

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the outer letters hold the rest
ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Henry Mancini, the American composer, writes Moon River, with a forceful argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Mancini wrote the song 'Moon River', which makes the surface ring true; 'Moon' is Io, one of Jupiter's moons.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is a Latin phrase meaning with even stronger reason.

clue.text: Arrival by alien going around Earth

indicators.note: going round turns the letters back on themselves

parts.note: arr is the abbreviation for arrival in timetables
ET is the film's extraterrestrial alien

explanation.surface: An alien arrives and circles the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' reverses ARRET to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for earth, used for the planet in science fiction.

clue.text: Top journalist hiding page that's filled out

indicators.note: the outer letters hide the page letter inside them

parts.note: plum means best, as in a plum job
ED, an editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A senior journalist conceals a page that has been completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumped means became fuller or rounder, so filled out.

clue.text: Limited time to cut song during album set back

indicators.note: the rest falls during the album, within it
set back means put in reverse order

parts.note: LP, long-player, is an album

indicators.note: the time letter cuts into the song, going inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: Limited studio time meant a song had to be cut from an album that was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts T into ARIA, making ARTIA; 'set back' reverses LP to PL, which holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means only in part, so limited in extent.

clue.text: Minor actor helping to win Oscar for project

parts.note: an extra is a background actor in a film

indicators.note: winning something takes it in, so the Oscar letter goes inside

parts.note: a helping of food is a plate
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film extra helps a star to win an Oscar for a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it is the radio code for O, placed inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project trends or data beyond known values.
